certs.emptyCertificatesHint: Add a certificate to get one browsers trust and install it on every node. Until then the cluster CA certificate is used.
certs.needAccount: To get a certificate, first add an ACME account (your account at the certificate authority) below.

deleteHint.account: The account is removed from the cluster. Certificates that use it must be deleted first.
deleteHint.dns: The DNS provider is removed. Certificates that use it must be deleted first.
deleteHint.certificate: The certificate is no longer renewed or installed. Listeners fall back to the internal CA certificate.

errors.name: Use lower-case letters, digits and hyphens (up to 63).
errors.url: Give the https:// URL of the ACME directory.
errors.tos: You must agree to the CA's terms of service.
errors.eab: Give both the EAB key id and the HMAC key, or neither.
errors.hook: The hook must be a file under /etc/orbivisor/acme-hooks/.

account.title: Add an ACME account
account.hint: The cluster creates the account key and registers with the CA right away.
account.tos: I agree to the CA's terms of service
account.checked: Account {{name}} is registered with the CA.

dns.title: Add a DNS provider
dns.hint: DNS-01 proves you own the domain by writing a temporary TXT record through this provider.
dns.zonesHint: Domains this provider runs, separated by commas (for example example.com). A certificate uses the provider of the zone its names belong to.

cert.title: Add a certificate
cert.hint: The leader orders it within a minute and renews it before it expires.
cert.namesHint: Domains to put in the certificate, separated by commas. {node} becomes the node name (per node only). *. names need DNS-01.
cert.keyHint: Default ECDSA P-256 — fast and supported by every browser. This build cannot make RSA keys.
cert.http01Missing: HTTP-01 needs the port 80 listener ([api] http_listen) on every node it covers. Missing on: {{nodes}}.

certs.intro: Gets HTTPS certificates that browsers trust, free from a certificate authority such as Let's Encrypt, and renews them automatically before they expire. Steps: 1. Add an ACME account → 2. (if needed) a DNS provider → 3. Add a certificate.
certs.emptyAccountsHint: The account at a certificate authority such as Let's Encrypt. All it needs is an email and accepting the terms.
certs.emptyDnsHint: Needed for wildcard names (*.example.com) or for nodes that the internet cannot reach on port 80. Otherwise you can skip it.

help.name: The name this page uses for it. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not at the start or end (for example le-prod).
help.directory: The certificate authority that issues the certificates. Default Let's Encrypt (free) — pick staging while testing to avoid rate limits.
help.url: The https:// ACME directory address of your in-house CA (step-ca and the like).
help.email: A contact address for the CA account. Optional. Let's Encrypt no longer sends expiry emails (since 2025), so use this cluster's alert rules (certificate expiring) for expiry notices.
help.eabHint: An account-binding key that ZeroSSL, Google and many in-house CAs require. Leave it empty for Let's Encrypt.
help.kid: The EAB key id from the CA's website. Enter it with the HMAC key.
help.caHint: Only for an in-house CA browsers do not trust yet: paste its root certificate (PEM). Usually leave it empty.
help.dnsName: The name for this DNS provider. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (not at the start or end).
help.dnsKind: Who runs DNS for your domain. If it is not listed, a hook script can connect an acme.sh or lego plugin.

dnsFields.api_token: A Cloudflare API token allowed to edit DNS. It is not shown again after saving.
dnsFields.zone_id: The Cloudflare zone id. Leave empty to find the zone by name.
dnsFields.access_key_id: The access key id of an AWS IAM user allowed to change Route 53.
dnsFields.secret_access_key: The secret key of that access key. It is not shown again after saving.
dnsFields.region: The AWS region. Empty means us-east-1.
dnsFields.hosted_zone_id: The Route 53 hosted zone id. Leave empty to find the zone by name.
dnsFields.server: The DNS server that accepts record changes (DNS UPDATE), such as 192.0.2.53:53.
dnsFields.key_name: The TSIG key name registered on the DNS server.
dnsFields.secret: That TSIG key's secret (base64). It is not shown again after saving.
dnsFields.zone: The DNS zone to write records in, such as example.com. Usually leave it empty.
dnsFields.url: The PowerDNS API address, such as http://192.0.2.10:8081.
dnsFields.api_key: The PowerDNS API key. It is not shown again after saving.
dnsFields.server_id: The PowerDNS server id. Empty means localhost.
dnsFields.path: The program that adds and removes the TXT record. Put it under /etc/orbivisor/acme-hooks/ on every node.

help.certName: The name for this certificate. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not at the start or end (for example api).
help.account: The ACME account that orders the certificate.
help.scope: Shared: every node uses one certificate (when users come in by one name). Per node: each node gets its own, by node name ({node}).
help.challenge: How you prove you own the domain. The default is DNS-01 when a DNS provider is set up, otherwise HTTP-01 (port 80). Use DNS-01 for wildcard names or private networks.
help.dns: The DNS provider that writes the TXT record for DNS-01.
help.profile: The kind of certificate the CA offers (for example Let's Encrypt's shortlived). Usually keep the CA default.
help.hmac: The EAB HMAC key from the CA. It is not shown again after saving.

certs.pageHint: Public certificates for the API and web listener from an ACME CA (Let's Encrypt, ZeroSSL, your own step-ca). The leader orders and renews them; nodes swap them in without a restart.
